label: medicine, treatment and hygiene
note: CLOSED BY CHAPTER 107, AND THE NOTE HELD. 'The symptoms are taught (ML-A1-LEX-27) and nothing that treats them is' -- LEX-27's five probe atoms were OPENED rather than trusted, because a note's characterisation of existing material is a claim and not a result. All five are named here rather than four: viSappu (FEEL-01), kshiiNaM (-02), vEdana (-03), cuma (-04) and pani (-05) are all taught headwords in chapter 63, so the claim is true. What the note does not say, and what the domain check found, is that vaidyan is taught at ML-C48-doctor (1310): the learner had the SYMPTOMS and the PERSON and nothing in between. Chapter 107 supplies the label's three parts, one word each -- marunnu (medicine, and the one word here Malayalam did not borrow), cikitsa (treatment) and vRtti (cleanliness) -- and carries forward C48's caveat that vaidyan usually points at a practitioner of the traditional medicine while the hospital doctor goes by the English word. vRtti is the EVERYDAY word and the lesson says so; Malayalam's formal word for hygiene-as-a-subject, SucitvaM, is NAMED in romanization only and is neither taught as a headword nor assessed. aashupatri and guLika were deliberately not added, and the reason is that NEITHER IS IN THIS POINT'S LABEL: the script-debt argument the first draft gave does not hold, since U+0D36 and U+0D33 already stand in 17 and 24 headwords. The one genuinely new piece of script here is the conjunct ta+sa in cikitsa -- every codepoint was already in use, but that PAIR was not, and ML-C107-chikitsa takes it apart against the chandrakkala join taught in chapter 1.
